Subject: Key ownership and HSM requirements - follow-up and proposed next steps

Hi Monique —

Great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through Acme Health's encryption and data residency constraints. Quick recap from our side and a list of clarifying questions so we can prepare an options matrix for you: 

Summary of asks you mentioned:
- Keys must be customer-managed and HSM-backed (FIPS 140-2/3 compliant)
- Keys must not be exportable from your Azure Key Vault (no plaintext key material leaves your boundary)
- Logs of key usage and model inference events must be retained for 7 years and made available for audit
- Data residency: inference in US-East only for PHI/PII workloads
- Proof points: SOC 2 report, encryption architecture diagram, and attestation of HSM usage

Clarifying questions (please confirm where you can):
1) Will Azure Key Vault (AKV) with HSM-protected keys be the canonical requirement, or would you accept an HSM-backed key in another cloud KMS?
2) For the logs you need — are you expecting push delivery to your SIEM (Splunk) or periodic S3/Blob exports?
3) Any procurement constraints (PO, master services agreement) or legal review timelines we should be aware of?

What we will deliver by next Friday (EOD Jun 12):
- Short options matrix: 1) Redwood Private + AKV integration (customer-managed keys) 2) Dedicated-hosted wrapped-key approach (hosted with key wrapping proxies) 3) On-prem/private HSM deployment details
- Compliance artifacts and a draft mutual action plan
- A proposed time for a technical deep-dive with Karthik and Marissa

Attachments: redwood-kms-options-matrix.xlsx (brief matrix)

If the above looks right I can schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week — propose Tue 6/15 or Wed 6/16 morning (US ED T).

Thanks — Laura

Laura —

Thanks for the recap, that matches our discussion. A few clarifications: 
- AKV (Azure Key Vault) with HSM-protected keys is our preferred and likely required approach. Keys must remain non-exportable.
- For logging, we need near-real-time push of key usage and session-level inference logs into our Splunk instance (Syslog or HTTPS ingestion). We also want daily blob backups (retention 7 years).
- Residency: yes, for any workloads involving PHI or PII we must keep inference in our US-East region. Non-PII training/experiments can run elsewhere but not production PHI.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + FIPS 140-2/3 statement required. We may ask for a third-party attestation depending on legal.

Procurement: Raj is leading procurement and will confirm PO cadence; we have a standard security questionnaire that I'll start filling but we may want a technical appendix.

Please include the architecture and any assumptions in the options matrix. We can do Tue 6/15 10:00 AM EDT for the deep-dive — Karbhik (our infra lead) will join.

Best,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Key ownership and HSM requirements - Acme follow-up (technical notes)

Laura / team —

Quick technical readout after a rapid sync with infra: 
- In-transit: Redwood already enforces TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS for customer connections. We will document cipher suites for their compliance team.
- At-rest: Model artifacts and token caches are encrypted at rest using host encryption. For customer-managed keys (CMK), the recommended path for strict no-export HSM requirement is Redwood Private deployed in their VPC with an AKV integration that performs KMS calls at inference time. In that architecture the plaintext key material never leaves the HSM. We call AKV for wrap/unwrap and/or encryption operations; Redwood holds only wrapped keys or ciphertext.
- Hosted product: we can support a wrapped-key pattern (customer supplies wrapped key material) but that does not satisfy a non-exportable HSM requirement in the same way as AKV HSM because the root HSM and key lifecycle are not under the customer's direct KMS control. For full no-export HSM guarantees, Private is strongly recommended.
- Logs: We can emit detailed key-usage and inference-level logs. For Splunk integration we can push via HTTPS/Syslog; alternatively we can deliver daily blobs to their Blob storage with signed manifests. We will include both options in the matrix.
- Compliance: we need to confirm FIPS/HSM attestation level from our HSM vendor (if Private uses a partner HSM) — action: Marissa to request vendor statement.

Limitations / risks:
- Network latency: AKV calls for every inference add RPC time. We can mitigate with short-lived cache tokens and locality (deploy Private in US-East).
- Operational: Key rotation and emergency rotation playbooks need agreement (who rotates, outage handling).

Next steps from infra side:
1) Draft architecture diagram (Marissa) with AKV integration and flow (client -> private runtime -> AKV)
2) Short performance impact estimate for AKV calls per request (I'll run microbenchmarks this week)
3) List of vendor compliance artifacts we can surface

I'll be on the deep-dive Tue 6/15 10am EDT.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Monique / team —

Thanks again for the quick responses. Attached are three items for your review before Tue's deep-dive: 
1) KMS option brief (PDF) — outlines 3 approaches and tradeoffs
2) Draft mutual action plan (DOCX) — high level milestones, owners, and proposed timelines
3) Compliance checklist with artifacts we can provide (Excel/attachments)

Short summary of the three approaches (high level):
- Redwood Private + AKV integration (recommended): Customer-managed HSM keys in AKV, no-export guarantee, logs to Splunk, US-East deployment. Best fit for production PHI/PII but requires Private deployment.
- Dedicated (reserved) in Redwood infra with wrapped-key pattern: Lower friction than Private but weaker no-export guarantees; good interim option for early pilots non-PHI.
- On-prem or air-gapped private deployment: Highest assurance, longer lead time and heavier ops.

Requested next actions from Acme:
- Confirm AKV as canonical KMS (or indicate acceptable alternatives)
- Provision a technical contact for Splunk ingestion (endpoint details)
- Confirm procurement path and target contract date so Priyom can align MAP milestones

We will bring a diagram, perf estimate, and vendor attestation to Tue's session. If anything in the attachments looks off, flag it and we'll update before the meeting.

Thanks — Laura
